mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is held constant for two consecutive months above 5.25%, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be positive due to reduced borrowing costs and increased equity discounting.
regime_hint: FOMC holds rates steady in a restrictive environment
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, the 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the 20-day returns during the preceding month when FEDFUNDS ≤ 5.25% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by at least 0.3 percentage points over the next month is associated with positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns due to labor market strengthening.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥ 2% in month t AND UNRATE decreases by ≥ 0.3pp in month t+1
regime_hint: Labor market transition from weakness to strength
failure_condition: Across 10 such labor-market turning points, the 20-day forward return is negative in at least 7 cases (binomial p < 0.3).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly industrial production index (INDPRO) exceeding 107.5 while consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) remains below 253 signals supply-side expansion without cost-of-living pressures, which tends to boost equity valuations and drive positive 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: In 5 such supply-side expansion episodes, the 60-day forward return is not positive in more than 2 episodes (binomial p < 0.4).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in retail sales (HOUST) of at least 3% for three consecutive months coincides with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5%, predicting a positive 20-day forward return as stronger demand supports equity risk premia.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases ≥ 3% for three consecutive months AND UNRATE < 3.5%
regime_hint: Resilient consumer demand in a low-unemployment environment
failure_condition: During 4 such demand cycles, the 20-day forward return is negative in more than 2 cycles (binomial p < 0.4).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the 12-month moving average of RSAFS (reserves) by at least 10% in a single month is interpreted as a signal of excess liquidity, which tends to produce negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns as investors anticipate a near-term rate hike.
candidate_trigger: 12-month RSAFS MA increases by ≥ 10% in month t
failure_condition: Over 8 such liquidity spikes, the 20-day forward return is not statistically lower than the 20-day return during the prior liquidity-neutral month (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly payrolls increase by at least 150,000 jobs but the unemployment rate (UNRATE) remains below 4%, the S&P 500 60-day forward return is expected to be negative due to the risk of over-heating labor markets and rising wage pressures.
failure_condition: Across 6 such labor-market expansion episodes, the 60-day forward return is not consistently negative (more than 2 episodes with positive returns; binomial p < 0.3).

mechanism_narrative: A long-term upward trend in the 12-month moving average of GDPC1 (real private demand) is associated with positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns, regardless of current levels or regimes, due to higher expected future cash flows.
failure_condition: Across 12 12-month GDPC1 up-trend episodes, the 20-day forward return is not positive in more than 80% of episodes (binomial p < 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: During a post-crisis normalization regime (defined by CPIAUCSL < 255 and UNRATE < 4.5%), a decline in the 3-month moving average of consumer prices (CPIAUCSL) by at least 0.5% is associated with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals deflationary pressure easing equity discounting.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL 3-month MA decreases by ≥ 0.5% AND regime: CPIAUCSL < 255 AND UNRATE < 4.5%
failure_condition: In 4 such regime-conditioned episodes, the 20-day forward return is not positive in more than 3 episodes (binomial p < 0.3).
